user_feedback.constraint: Keep original outer dimensions; vary thread geometry without increasing head, length, nut body or shaft outside diameter.

findings: Both prior profiles were already trapezoidal; switching names to ACME is not by itself a geometry improvement.
Standard ACME uses 29 degree included angle. A custom wider included angle reduces radial overhang per layer when printed with the axis vertical.
A1 mini has an official 0.12 mm Fine profile for a 0.4 mm nozzle.
Malformed as-printed threads require examining overhang formation, speed, cooling and extrusion rather than assuming a clearance-only problem.

axial_section_estimates.method: Radial layer step = layer height × radial flank run / axial flank rise; simple axial-section estimate, not a physical failure diagnosis or exact helical toolpath calculation.

decision: Test original-size 8 mm OD / 3 mm pitch custom 90-degree included trapezoid, 0.8 mm depth, 0.6 mm crest and unchanged 0.30 mm female radial clearance; 0.12 mm layers, slower wall speeds and cooling. This is not standard ACME.

sources.role: Primary CAD-library documentation: trapezoidal and ACME angle definitions.
Official Bambu A1 mini Fine profile, inspected online and in installed Bambu Studio.
Author-published FDM-oriented trapezoidal profiles; independent precedent, not A1 mini validation.
Firsthand A-series thread-failure discussion; anecdotal recommendations for thin layers/cooling, and author-reported calibration fix. Not an official recipe or proof of this case.
